title: Atelier Scheduling Note on Relief Where Production Started Late
content:
# Atelier Scheduling Note on Relief Where Production Started Late

On a commission under Belrose Design Studio Custom Commissions, the fraction at which the figure reached for a metal market repricing is taken turns on whether a deposit has been received and on how long the piece has gone without entering production since that deposit.

## The fractions

1. Where a deposit has been received on the commission and the piece had not gone into production within the studio's long start-delay days, which are 90 calendar days, of the deposit being received, the figure reached is taken at the studio's long start-delay fraction, which is 0.5.
2. Where a deposit has been received and the piece had not gone into production within the studio's start-delay days, which are 45 calendar days, of the deposit being received, but within its long start-delay days, the figure reached is taken at the studio's start-delay fraction, which is 0.75.
3. Otherwise the figure reached stands as it is.

## How the days are read

The date the deposit was received is the date of the latest deposit entry booked to the commission; the days are counted from that date to the day the repricing is booked. The piece has gone into production where the date production began stands on the commission, and has not where that date is empty; where the piece has gone into production, the figure reached stands as it is.

## A day-count reading (hypothetical)

A commission whose deposit was received on the 1st of January, with no date of production beginning standing on it.

| Repricing booked | Days since the deposit | Fraction |
|---|---|---|
| The 10th of February | 40 | The figure reached stands as it is |
| The 16th of February | 46 | 0.75 |
| The 1st of April | 90 | 0.75 |
| The 2nd of April | 91 | 0.5 |
